references.text: God sends Moses to Pharaoh to lead the children of Israel out of Egypt, the same mission that is repeated here.
Moses and Aaron go to Pharaoh and ask him to let the people of Israel leave, as preparation for this repeated mission.
God repeats the command that Pharaoh must let the children of Israel leave his land.
The Lord tells Moses that Pharaoh will eventually send the people out of Egypt.
Fulfillment of God's command: Pharaoh sends the children of Israel out of Egypt.
The psalmist reminds us that God sent Moses as His servant to Egypt.
Stephen's speech refers to how God sent Moses to free Israel from Egypt.
By faith, Moses left Egypt without fearing the king's wrath, which is connected to his confrontation with Pharaoh.
The command in 6:11 is confirmed as fulfilled action in 6:27, underscoring God's faithfulness to His word.
6:11 sets in motion the process that 7:4 predicts will lead to liberation through judgment.
6:29 confirms the divine authority ("I am the Lord") behind the command given in 6:11.
6:1 promises the result that 6:11 requires action to initiate.
4:22 provides the theological basis (Israel as God's firstborn) for the requirement in 6:11.
9:1 shows the continuity of God's demand from 6:11 throughout the confrontation with Pharaoh.
